section_summary: These pages cover negotiations over the limits of Japanese fishing, requests for Japanese whaling statistics, and a private proposal to use chartered vessels for whaling and tuna fishing. The final memorandum weighs whether SCAP should pursue fishing rights off Kamchatka before Japanese peace treaty discussions.

subfiles.title: FEC action on fishing policy
subfiles.about: Proposes a formula for interpreting fishing restrictions near Allied jurisdictions.
subfiles.summary: Whitman proposes consultations over the meaning of “near” to help secure FEC support without setting a fixed distance.

subfiles.title: Request for Japanese whaling statistics
subfiles.about: Requests prompt collection of 1946–47 Japanese whaling data for the International Bureau for Whaling Statistics.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy seeks catch, oil, by-product, vessel and station data for Japanese whaling at Bonin Island.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Japanese whaling statistics
subfiles.about: Advises that SCAP sent the requested whaling information directly to Sandefjord.
subfiles.summary: SCAP transmitted the data by radio to the International Bureau for Whaling Statistics.

subfiles.title: Confidential proposal to charter vessels for tuna fishing and whaling
subfiles.to: United States Maritime Commission, Operations Bureau
subfiles.about: Seeks terms for chartering two vessels for a Japanese crewed tuna and whale-meat venture.
subfiles.summary: Ekdale describes plans to learn Japanese South Pacific tuna-fishing methods and use two refrigerated vessels for tuna and Antarctic whale meat. He asks whether the Maritime Commission would support the venture and offer a charter rate reflecting its risks. The proposal would require Japanese and SCAP approval.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Japanese whaling reports to Oslo
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Oslo
subfiles.about: Forwards SCAP reports on coastal and Bonin Island whaling for delivery to Sandefjord.
subfiles.summary: The mission is asked to send two SCAP whaling reports to the International Bureau for Whaling Statistics.

subfiles.title: Cable to POLAD re Japanese fishers
subfiles.about: Explains a proposed cable on possible negotiations for Japanese fishing rights off Kamchatka.
subfiles.summary: Whitman weighs FEC pressure, Soviet opposition and peace treaty timing; negotiations depend on favorable prospects and Japanese readiness.
